rows.en:
"What a load of crap that story was."
Shindo was fuming.
Arai had walked straight out of the room and showed no sign of coming back.
Why on earth {f:had he|had he} said something like that?
That one of {f:us|us} would become the doll's sacrifice...
That was taking a joke {f:way|way} too far.{p}

"I'm outta here."
Shindo quickly gathered up his things and left the room.
{f:I|I} had no right to stop him.
Looking around, I could tell everyone else wanted to go home too.
And there was no sign of the seventh person coming.
Then again, even if the seventh showed up now, the mood was hardly right for carrying on.
What {f:should|should} I do?{p}Would it be better to {f:just|just} end it here?
End it here
Stay a little longer

{f:Yes|Yes}, it {f:would|would} be better to end it after all.
There {f:was|was} no point in staying here any longer.
"Well then, everyone.
Thank you very much for today."
{f:I|I} bowed to those who were still there, and let that be my closing remark.{p}

After everyone had gone, {f:I|I} was the last one out, and I locked up the room.
{f:I|I} hadn't really taken the doll story to heart.
That sort of thing is common {f:enough|enough} in scary stories.
I'd heard {f:of|of} stories like that, ones that end by leaving whoever is there with a nasty feeling.{p}

Like the kind where the teller speaks in a hushed voice, building it up quietly, then shouts right at the climax to make you jump.
Or the kind that ends by saying misfortune will fall on whoever heard it.
It had to be one of those.
...But if I was thinking about it this much, didn't that mean {f:I|I} was bothered by it after all{f:?|?}{p}
I made sure the club room door was locked, and was just about to head home when it happened.{p}

"{c}{f:|...}"
Someone called my name from behind me.
It was {f:a|a} woman's voice, trembling with sadness.
{f:My|My} legs shook with fear.{p}Should I turn around{f:?|?}
Turn around
Don't turn around
{f:I|I} slowly looked back over my shoulder.{p}
"...{f:Oh|Geez}, {f:it's just you|it was only you}, Fukuzawa."

There stood Fukuzawa, looking troubled.
"Don't you '{f:oh, it's just you|geez}' me.
And here I waited so we could walk home together."
Hearing the deflated sound of {f:my|my} voice, she puffed out her cheeks a little and pouted.
"Sorry, sorry.
I didn't mean it like that. I just {f:got|got} mixed up for a second."
"Mixed up with what?"
"With what...?"{p}

"You're bothered by that story earlier, aren't you?"
She grinned like a mischievous kid.
"What about you, Fukuzawa?
Weren't you the one too scared to walk home alone, so you waited for {f:me|me}?"
{f:I|I} grinned right back at her.
"Hehe... Actually, yeah.
Now that we've gotten to know each other like this, you know?
Let's go home together."{p}What {f:should|should} I do?
Go home together
Go home alone

"{f:Yeah|Sure}, {f:let's|let's}."
"Great!"
She came up to {f:me|me}, looking happy.
Side by side, the two of us walked down the deserted hallway of the new school building.{p}

"It's already past eight, huh."
Fukuzawa peered into a classroom beside us and was surprised by the clock on the wall.
So it had {f:already|already} gotten that late.
When {f:I|I} came to the club room, it had looked like it could rain any minute, but the weather {f:seemed to have|seemed to have} held.
"{f:We sure stayed late, huh|We stayed really late, didn't we}."
"{f:Yeah|Mm-hm}."
After that, the conversation went nowhere.{p}

{f:I|I} didn't know what to talk about and kept searching for something to say.
I had hoped that cheerful Fukuzawa might come up with a topic, but maybe that was a bit too convenient a wish.
Still, having Fukuzawa there was a real help to {f:me|me}, {f:honestly|honestly}.
After hearing all those scary stories, I don't think {f:I|I}'d have had quite enough courage to walk home from school alone.
Without meaning to, I quickened my pace down the hallway, which felt longer than usual.
The only sound was our footsteps echoing down the hall, so they sounded terribly loud, and I even had the illusion that a whole crowd of people was following behind us.
Was all of this just the fear Arai had planted in me{f:?|?}{p}

...{f:Huh|What}?
What {f:is that|is that}?
I could see a figure at the far end of the hallway.
It looked like it was beckoning to us, waving us over...
What {f:should|should} I do?{p}Wouldn't it be better {f:not|not} to go over there{f:?|?}
Keep going straight ahead
Turn back and take another way

"Hey, Fukuzawa."
{f:I|I} tugged at Fukuzawa's sleeve.
"What's wrong?"
"Why don't we take a different way, {f:huh|okay}?"{p}

Fukuzawa looked at {f:me|me} blankly.
It {f:must|must} have struck her as really odd, {f:me|me} suddenly saying something like that.
"Why?"
"...What do you mean, why?
I've got a bad feeling {f:about this|about this}.
Like we shouldn't keep going straight ahead..."
Fukuzawa put a hand over her mouth, as if she were about to burst out laughing.{p}

"It's fine.
{c}{f:|}, you're a real scaredy-cat, you know that?
It's okay, it's okay.
I'm right here with you."
With that, she took {f:my|my} hand and started marching ahead.
Somehow, she was {f:incredibly|incredibly} strong.
Wasn't this {f:bad|bad}?{p}Wouldn't it be a bad idea to {f:keep|keep} walking like this?
Shake off her hand
Keep following her

"{f:Stop it|Stop it}!"
Before I knew it, {f:I|I} was screaming so loudly it surprised even me.{p}

"...It's okay.
But that really surprised me.
I never thought you'd be this much of a scaredy-cat, {c}{f:|}.
Sorry for pushing you like that.
Okay, I get it. Let's go a different way."
Acting like she was the older one, Fukuzawa patted {f:me|me} on the shoulder.
It was really embarrassing.
Sure, {f:I|I} was a scaredy-cat, but being pitied by {f:a girl|someone} my own age made me strangely want to make excuses.
Even so, I really didn't have the courage to push on down this hallway.
For now, I decided not to argue and to accept Fukuzawa's kindness.{p}

{f:I|I} turned back to go home another way.
The long way round is the safest way.
That was {f:the|the} best thing to do.
...{f:But|But}.
{f:I|I} stopped in my tracks again.{p}

There was something {f:up|up} ahead, too.
{f:I|I} was trapped between two unknown figures.
And {f:this one|this one} was slowly closing in on {f:me|me}!
{f:It|It} came toward me, twisting its body as if hopping, moving in jerky fits.
Just like a puppet on strings...
A doll?
{f:I|I} gasped.
Looked at {f:a certain|a certain} way, {f:that thing|that thing} {f:really|really} was a doll.
Surely it wasn't the doll Arai had been talking about...{p}

rows.en:
"...{c}{f:|}.
{c}{f:|}!"
Fukuzawa's voice snapped {f:me|me} back to my senses.
Fukuzawa was shaking {f:me|me} by the shoulders.
"What's wrong? You're drenched in sweat."{p}

Then she peered worriedly into {f:my|my} face.
When I looked, {f:that thing|that thing} was gone.
{f:My|My} shirt was soaked through, as if it had been dipped in water.
I was breathing very hard.
"Hey, are you okay? Maybe you should sit down for a bit?"
Fukuzawa asked me again.
"I'm fine now{f:, really|, really}. Come on, let's go."{p}

I may have said that, but that unknown figure was burned into {f:my|my} mind and wouldn't leave.
...Had Fukuzawa seen it{f:, I wondered|, I wondered}?
What should I do?
Should I ask her?{p}No, wouldn't it be better {f:not|not} to ask?
Ask her
Keep quiet

If Fukuzawa had seen it too, then it wasn't a hallucination.
It would mean someone really had been there.
{f:I|I} worked up my nerve and brought it up.
"Fukuzawa. Just now, {f:wasn't|wasn't} there someone at the far end of the hallway?"{p}

Fukuzawa's eyes went wide for an instant, then narrowed as she looked at {f:me|me} suspiciously.
She hadn't seen anything.
{f:I|I} quickly took it back.
"No, I mean, {f:I|I} didn't actually see anything{f:, you know|}.
We heard all those scary stories, {f:right|right}?
So I'm just kind of worn out..."{p}

"Are you really okay?"
Fukuzawa was looking at {f:me|me} like I was some kind of guinea pig.
It {f:seemed|seemed} best not to touch on this any further.
"Let's go home.
If a teacher catches us in a place like this, who knows how much trouble we'll be in."
"You're right. Let's hurry."
{f:We|We} left the school as if we were running from something.{p}

{f:It must|It must} have been {f:my imagination|my imagination} after all.
{f:I|I} told myself that over and over, trying to convince myself.
I'd only seen that unknown thing for {f:an|an} instant, after all.
I'd been really tired, so I'd seen something that {f:wasn't|wasn't} there.
...{f:But|But} I was soon forced to realize just how wrong I was.
{f:This was|Little did I know this was} only the beginning of the terror.{p}

...The next day, {f:I|I} was called in by Hino.
I had to report on what happened yesterday.
After school, when I went to the club room, Hino was waiting.
"Hey, {a}. Good work yesterday.
So, how'd it go?"{p}What {f:should|should} I talk about?
The scary stories I heard yesterday
The seventh person not showing up
Our plans from here on

"Well.
I think it went pretty well overall.
Still, everyone sure knows a lot of scary stories.
{f:I|I} was really impressed.
...But what is the deal with Kazama?
He's, like, insanely dangerous, or weird, or... someone who's just beyond all common sense."{p}

"Ahahaha. Sorry, sorry.
I figured you'd get worn out if it was nothing but scary stories, so I asked him to do it."
Hino laughed cheerfully, as if he'd seen {f:my|my} words coming from the start.
"Oh, so that's what it was.
That's mean of you, Hino."{p}
"So, how did the rest go?"

Hino reacted as if to say 'oops' and clapped his hands.
"Right, that.
I completely forgot to tell you, but that was my mistake.
I thought I'd asked seven people, but when I thought about it later, I'd only asked six.
I meant to apologize later, but it slipped my mind.
Sorry, sorry."
What an anticlimactic ending.
Who'd have thought Hino had simply forgotten to invite one person?
I was so let down I couldn't even {f:think of|think of} a reply.{p}

"Don't make that face, {a}.
I'm apologizing, aren't I?
So, how did the rest go?"

"Well.
It's less about yesterday and more about our plans from here on. I was wondering how to proceed.
{f:I really|I really} think it'd be better to make the article fun to look at too, using lots of illustrations and photos, not just text.
I never imagined our school had this many scary stories, and I bet nobody else knows either."{p}

Hino listened to {f:my|my} proposal, looking pleased.
"I see. Now that's reassuring to hear.
Alright, I'll leave the article to you.
Do it however you like, and make it a masterpiece."
{f:I|I} felt a little proud to be entrusted with such an unexpectedly big role.{p}
"So, how did the rest go?"

"So, which story scared you the most?
Don't tell me it was Kazama's."
"No way. Not a chance.
Sure, I was surprised at first while listening, but his story was total nonsense.
Let's see, the one that scared {f:me|me} the most was... I'd have to say Arai's{f:, I guess|}."{p}

Opinions probably differ on which story is the scariest.
But for {f:me|me}, what left the strongest impression was Arai's way of talking, his atmosphere, and above all that ending, which left me feeling {f:so|so} awful.{p}

"Arai's story? What kind of story?"
Hino tilted his head, looking puzzled.
It {f:seemed|seemed} Hino hadn't heard what kind of story Arai would tell either.
Then again, which story to tell had probably been left up to them.
{f:I|I} gave him a quick summary of Arai's story.{p}

"So this Arai guy became the doll's sacrifice, huh."
Hino nodded to himself, as if he finally got it.
What {f:was|was} Hino talking about?
"No, that's not it.
Arai was the one who told the story. He didn't become any sacrifice.
Though at the end, he did say one of {f:us|us} would become the sacrifice, so maybe..."{p}

"Hold on a sec. Who's Arai?"
Hino cut in, looking puzzled.{p}

"Who's Arai?"
Hino's words made no sense to {f:me|me} at all.
"...What do you mean, who?
You invited him, didn't you, Hino..."
"I didn't invite anybody named Arai.
Forget inviting, I don't even know anyone by that name.
Were you dreaming or something?"{p}

"But..."
"That's right.
You're getting dreams and reality all mixed up.
The six I invited were Kazama and Shindo, plus Iwashita, Kiyose, Hosoda, and Fukuzawa."
"Kiyose?"
The name Kiyose didn't ring a bell.
There had definitely been no one like that there.{p}

"Kiyose. Kiyose.
Naomichi Kiyose, from Class 3-F.
He didn't show up?"
Hino asked {f:me|me}, looking a little unnerved himself.
"...Right."
{f:I|I} could only nod.
After all, {f:I|I} didn't know anyone like that.{p}

"So there really was a guy called Arai?"
"Yes."
{f:I|I} nodded firmly.
It {f:wasn't|wasn't} a dream.
{f:I could even ask the others to back me up|The others would say so too}.
{f:That's it|That's it}.
I {f:just|just} had to check with the others.{p}
Who should I go see?
Reiko Fukuzawa
Reiko Fukuzawa
Akemi Iwashita
Akemi Iwashita
Makoto Shindo
Makoto Shindo
Nozomu Kazama
Nozomu Kazama
Tomoharu Hosoda
Tomoharu Hosoda
Naomichi Kiyose
Naomichi Kiyose

I decided to go see Iwashita.
But after that whole business yesterday, she had gone home partway through, and somehow I felt awkward about going to her.
Still, I had to confirm that Arai existed.
I tracked down Iwashita's classroom and peeked inside.{p}

There was no sign of Iwashita.
I asked a girl who was standing near the doorway.
"...Um, is Iwashita here?"
"Oh.
Akemi? She's absent today.
Do you need something?"
"Ah, no.
Sorry to bother you."{p}
{f:I|I} decided to go see Iwashita.{p}

I found her classroom and peeked in. Iwashita was leaning on a desk with her hands, lost in some vague thought.
"Iwashita!"
When {f:I|I} called out, Iwashita slowly turned around.
Then, wearing that chilling, eerie smile of hers, she beckoned {f:me|me} over.{p}

{f:I|I} stood beside her and spoke in a low whisper.
"...Um, it's about Arai."
"The doll story?"
If Iwashita was bringing up the doll story, then {f:it really|it really} hadn't been my dream.
{f:Iwashita|Iwashita, too,} had heard Arai's story{f:.|!}
"No, more than that... I just asked Hino about it a moment ago.
Apparently he never invited anyone called Arai.
Worse, he says he doesn't even know anyone like that."
{f:I|I} was hoping for some reaction from Iwashita, {f:but|but} she was perfectly calm and not the least bit surprised.{p}
"Oh, is that so? Well, what does it matter?
After all, I've been seeing dolls this whole time."{p}

"Huh★"
"This world is full of dolls.
Everyone but me is a doll.
You're a doll too.
...Look, there's a doll behind you as well."{p}
Relieved, I turned back to Iwashita. She was smiling like a little devil.{p}
I couldn't tell how much of what she said was serious.{p}
{f:I|I} decided to look for Kazama.{p}

I looked, but he wasn't there.
I was sure this was the place, but...{p}

"Boo!"
Suddenly, two hands covered my eyes from behind.
"I am the devil's messenger."
The words were whispered right in my ear.
"Kazama!
Quit fooling around."
I shook off the hands and turned around.{p}

"Aaah!"
There stood a giant cockroach...
Yeah, right. There's no way something like that exists.
I pulled off the tasteless mask shaped like a giant cockroach.{p}

Kazama's smirking face emerged from inside the cockroach.
"Ahaha... You're as boring as ever, you know.
At this rate, you'll never be a hit with the girls like I am.
And here I was, going to teach you how to get girls."
Talking with this guy always throws me off.
"Don't tell me you're mad that I left partway through?
Come on, nobody likes a guy who can't take a joke."
So he really had just gone home early.
People don't just suddenly vanish.
"I know.
As a special favor, I'll teach you a gag that'll make the girls love you.
Right now it's a special bargain, just five thousand yen.
So, how about one?"{p}
"That's enough, thanks."{p}
I ran out of the classroom without listening to Kazama.{p}
{f:I|I} headed for Kazama's classroom.{p}

I looked, but he wasn't there.
I was sure this was the place, but...{p}

"Boo!"
Suddenly, two hands covered my eyes from behind.
"I am the devil's messenger."
The words were whispered right in my ear.
"Kazama!
Quit fooling around."
{f:I|I} shook off the hands and turned around.{p}
"That's enough, thanks."{p}
{f:I|I} ran out of the classroom without listening to Kazama.{p}
{f:I|I} decided to look for Fukuzawa.{p}

Fukuzawa looked worried again.
She seemed to be connecting this with the way {f:I|I} had acted last night.
"...What's wrong? Is your head okay?"
"Just answer {f:me, okay|me}.
{f:We|We} definitely heard the doll story from Arai{f:, right|, didn't we}?"{p}
Fukuzawa, perhaps overwhelmed by how intense {f:I|I} was, gave a small nod.{p}
{f:Just as I thought|So I was right}, Fukuzawa had seen him too{f:.|.}{p}
{f:I|I} decided to go see Shindo.{p}

When I went to Shindo's classroom, no one was there.
It {f:seemed|looked like} everyone had already gone home.{p}

{f:It can't be helped|Oh well, it can't be helped}.
{f:Guess I'll give up on Shindo|I'll just have to give up on Shindo}.{p}
{f:I|I} decided to look for Hosoda.{p}

"Bwahahahaha... Hosoda?
Hosoda's probably in the john, ain't he?
That guy's always hangin' out in the john.
Go look in the toilets!
Bwahahahaha..."{p}

"Whoa!"
Just as I turned to leave the classroom, {f:I|I} slammed into Hosoda's huge body.
Hosoda was wiping his hands on a handkerchief, beaming.
Apparently he had just finished his business in the toilet.{p}
Hosoda was grinning from ear to ear.{p}

"Hey, if it isn't {a}{f:|}!
I'm so happy! Did you come to see me?
We really are best friends!"
With that, he threw his arms around {f:my|my} shoulders.{p}

At that, Hosoda let go of {f:me|me}, and suddenly he looked creeped out.
"Please don't bring up that story.
I'm trying hard to forget it myself.
Still, that Arai has a nasty streak, doesn't he...
Telling a story like that and scaring everyone."
"So you did hear Arai's story!"
When {f:I|I} pressed him, Hosoda backed away as if startled.{p}

"What's gotten into you, {a}{f:|}...?"
"Hosoda, did you know Arai from before?"
"...No, I only met him for the first time yesterday.
We're in the same year, but I'd never seen Arai before.
Then again, there are so many students at this school, so I guess it can't be helped."{p}

Hosoda tilted his head, puzzled.
"Thank you very much."{p}
Saying only that, {f:I|I} left Hosoda's classroom.{p}

"Um, is there someone named Kiyose in this class?"
"That's me. Why?"
A voice came from the corner of the classroom, and someone walked over.
So he was Kiyose{f:?|?}
"Who are you?"
"Um, {f:I'm|I'm} {b} {a}, from the newspaper club, and..."
"Sorry!"
Before {f:I|I} could finish introducing myself, he suddenly pressed his palms together and bowed his head deeply.{p}

"Man, you're Hino's junior, right?
I'm sorry.
Yesterday I suddenly came down with a fever.
It got so bad that I went home early.
I feel bad about it.
Next time I'll tell you my very best scary story... What's wrong, spacing out like that?"
"Oh, {f:no|no}, {f:sorry|I'm sorry}."
This time it was {f:me|me} bowing my head to Kiyose.{p}
Find out
Forget about it

{f:I|I} made the rounds of every second-year classroom.
And I learned one fact.
There was no one named Shoji Arai among the second-years.
{f:In that case|Then}, who {f:was he|was he}?
I'd search again.
Maybe one of the classrooms had been empty when I checked.
{f:I|I} must have {f:overlooked him|missed him}.
Whatever it took, I {f:had to|had to} find out.{p}

"{a}!"
Just as {f:I|I} was about to go around the second-year classrooms again, a voice behind me called out to stop me.{p}

Shindo came up to {f:me|me} and muttered with a sigh.
"...So, how'd it go?
Did you find Arai?"
Shindo too...?
Shindo couldn't find him either{f:?|?}
{f:I|I} honestly shook my head.
"...I see.
Come over here a sec."{p}

"Looks like there's no guy named Shoji Arai in the second year at our school."
Shindo's words completely shattered {f:my|my} faint hope.{p}

"...Yesterday, after all that, it kept bugging me, so I did some digging.
And guess what.
Looks like that doll story he told is actually true.
Apparently every year, one person always gets sacrificed and dies.
So I went looking for Arai to beat the crap outta him for saying that stuff, but he's nowhere to be found.
There's no such guy among our students.{p}

...Hey, {a}.
Are you listening to me?"{p}

...{f:I|I} had bigger things to worry about.
Something was visible behind Shindo.
It was a doll, no doubt about it.
A life-sized doll with a brown face was staring at {f:me|me} through the classroom window.
"What're you lookin' at, {a}?"
Bothered by where {f:I|I} was looking, Shindo turned around.
But Shindo apparently couldn't see {f:it|it}; he just kept glancing all around.{p}

"What's wrong with you, {a}!"
By the time Shindo shook me, the doll was already gone.
"...It's nothing.
Hearing your story just made me feel a little sick, that's all."
Shindo seemed to believe {f:me|me}{f:.|.}{p}

"I see.
Be careful.
Anyway, don't believe a word that guy said.
There's a ton of students at this school.
No way one of us is gonna end up the sacrifice."
It sounded less like he was saying it to {f:me|me} and more like Shindo was telling it to himself.
With that, Shindo clapped {f:me|me} on the shoulder and walked off.{p}

...It started after that.
That {f:I|I} began seeing the doll often.
A life-sized doll with a brown face and big eyes.
It was quite different from the one in Arai's story, but he'd said its appearance depends on who sees it, so the doll in front of {f:me|me} right now must be the one{f:.|.}
For a while now, the doll has been standing silently in a corner of {f:my|my} room.
At first I only saw the doll at school, but now it comes all the way to {f:my|my} house.
And the number of times {f:I|I} saw the doll grew by the day.{p}
Quietly wait for death like this
Try my best to connect with the doll
Talk to someone about it
Try going to school once more
